contentHtml:
mutton biryani greets you with an aromatic embrace as tender pieces of lamb bathed in creamy yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, and a medley of warming spices simmer gently alongside toasted onions and chopped tomatoes. Each layer of fragrant basmati rice, braided with saffron-infused milk and garnished with crisp fried onions and fresh mint, tells a story of love and tradition. As the pot lids huff steam and flavors meld, your home transforms into a bustling spice market. One golden spoonful reveals a tapestry of flavors that’s both comforting and celebratory. Invite friends, savor the journey, and create memories around this timeless feast.

Why You’ll Love This mutton biryani

  • Rich, aromatic flavors that transport you to culinary heaven.
  • Perfectly tender mutton that melts in your mouth.
  • Layered with fragrant basmati rice for a delightful texture.
  • Customizable with your favorite spices and ingredients.
  • A crowd-pleaser that brings family and friends together.

Ingredients
  

Meat

Rice

Vegetables
  • 2 large onions thinly sliced
  • 2 medium tomatoes chopped
Dairy
  • 1/2 cup yogurt adds creaminess
Spices
  • 2 tbsp ginger-garlic paste for flavor
  • 4 pieces green chilies slit for heat
  • 1/4 cup fresh coriander leaves chopped
  • 1/4 cup mint leaves chopped
  • 4 pieces cloves for aroma
  • 4 pieces green cardamoms for aroma
  • 1 inch cinnamon stick for aroma
  • 1 piece bay leaf for aroma
  • 1 tsp turmeric powder for color
  • 2 tsp red chili powder for spice
  • 2 tsp biryani masala for authentic taste
  • 1/4 cup ghee or oil for richness
  • to taste salt to taste
  • 3 cups water for cooking

Equipment

  • 1 Heavy-bottomed pot For cooking the biryani
  • 1 Separate pot For parboiling the rice

Method
 

Preparation
  1. Wash and soak the basmati rice for 30 minutes. Drain and set aside.
Cooking
  1. Heat ghee or oil in a heavy-bottomed pot. Add the whole spices and sauté until fragrant.
  2. Add sliced onions and cook until golden brown. Remove half for garnish.
  3. Stir in ginger-garlic paste, green chilies, chopped tomatoes, and cook until tomatoes soften.
  4. Add mutton pieces, turmeric, red chili powder, biryani masala, and salt. Cook on medium heat until mutton is lightly browned.
  5. Mix in yogurt, half of the chopped coriander and mint leaves. Cook covered for 15–20 minutes until mutton is tender.
  6. In a separate pot, bring 3 cups water to a boil. Add drained rice and a pinch of salt. Parboil the rice (about 70% cooked), then drain.
  7. Layer the parboiled rice over the cooked mutton. Sprinkle the reserved fried onions, remaining coriander, mint leaves, and a drizzle of ghee.
  8. Cover tightly, reduce heat to low, and cook on dum (steam) for 20–25 minutes.
  9. Turn off the heat and let it rest for 10 minutes. Gently fluff the rice before serving.

How to Make Mutton Biryani

Get ready to embark on a flavorful journey with this authentic mutton biryani recipe! With a preparation time of 30 minutes, cooking time of about 1 hour, and an additional resting time of 10 minutes, you’ll have a delicious meal ready to impress your family and friends.

Step 1: Wash and Soak the Rice

Wash and soak the basmati rice for 30 minutes. Drain and set aside.

Step 2: Sauté Whole Spices

Heat ghee or oil in a heavy-bottomed pot. Add the whole spices and sauté until fragrant.

Step 3: Cook Onions

Add sliced onions and cook until golden brown. Remove half for garnish.

Step 4: Add Ginger-Garlic and Tomatoes

Stir in ginger-garlic paste, green chilies, chopped tomatoes, and cook until tomatoes soften.

Step 5: Cook Mutton

Add mutton pieces, turmeric, red chili powder, biryani masala, and salt. Cook on medium heat until mutton is lightly browned.

Step 6: Mix in Yogurt and Herbs

Mix in yogurt, half of the chopped coriander and mint leaves. Cook covered for 15–20 minutes until mutton is tender.

Step 7: Parboil the Rice

In a separate pot, bring 3 cups water to a boil. Add drained rice and a pinch of salt. Parboil the rice (about 70% cooked), then drain.

Step 8: Layer the Biryani

Layer the parboiled rice over the cooked mutton. Sprinkle the reserved fried onions, remaining coriander, mint leaves, and a drizzle of ghee.

Step 9: Cook on Dum

Cover tightly, reduce heat to low, and cook on dum (steam) for 20–25 minutes.

Step 10: Rest and Serve

Turn off the heat and let it rest for 10 minutes. Gently fluff the rice before serving.

Recipe Snapshot

Pro Tips for Making mutton biryani

  • Marinate the mutton overnight for deeper flavor.
  • Use basmati rice for the perfect texture and aroma.
  • Layer the rice and meat gently to avoid breaking the grains.
  • Add a few saffron strands for a beautiful color and fragrance.
  • Let the biryani rest after cooking for enhanced flavors.

How to Serve this mutton biryani

  • Garnish with fresh cilantro and mint for a burst of flavor.
  • Serve with cooling raita made from yogurt, cucumber, and spices.
  • Pair with a tangy salad of onions, tomatoes, and lemon juice.
  • Enjoy with a side of spicy pickle for an extra kick.
  • Offer warm naan or paratha to scoop up the biryani.
  • Complement with a refreshing mint lemonade or lassi.

Make Ahead and Storage

Storing and enjoying your mutton biryani later is easy!

Storing Leftovers

  • Allow biryani to cool to room temperature.
  • Transfer to an airtight container.
  • Store in the refrigerator for up to 3 days.
  • Label with the date for easy tracking.

Freezing

  • Cool biryani completely before freezing.
  • Use freezer-safe containers or heavy-duty freezer bags.
  • Remove excess air from bags to prevent freezer burn.
  • Freeze for up to 3 months for best quality.

Reheating

  • Thaw overnight in the refrigerator if frozen.
  • Reheat in a pot over low heat, adding a splash of water.
  • Stir occasionally to ensure even heating.
  • Microwave in short intervals, covered, for quick reheating.

FAQs

Here’s a helpful FAQ about this recipe:

1. What is mutton biryani made of?

Mutton biryani is a flavorful dish made primarily of marinated mutton, basmati rice, and a blend of aromatic spices. The mutton is typically cooked with yogurt, onions, garlic, ginger, and various spices like cardamom, cloves, and saffron, which infuse the rice with rich flavors. The dish is often garnished with fried onions, fresh herbs, and boiled eggs, making it a complete and satisfying meal.

2. Is mutton biryani sheep or goat?

Mutton biryani traditionally refers to meat from mature sheep, but in many regions, it is often made with goat meat as well. The term ‘mutton’ can vary in meaning depending on the country; in some places, it may refer to goat meat. Regardless of the source, both types of meat can yield a delicious biryani when cooked properly.

3. What is the meaning of mutton biryani?

The term ‘mutton biryani’ combines ‘mutton,’ which refers to the meat of mature sheep, and ‘biryani,’ a mixed rice dish originating from the Indian subcontinent. Biryani is known for its layers of marinated meat and fragrant rice, often cooked together to create a harmonious blend of flavors. Thus, mutton biryani signifies a rice dish featuring mutton as the primary protein, seasoned with spices and herbs.

4. What is the difference between lamb biryani and mutton biryani?

The main difference between lamb biryani and mutton biryani lies in the age of the animal from which the meat is sourced. Lamb refers to meat from young sheep, typically under one year old, while mutton comes from older sheep. As a result, lamb biryani tends to have a milder flavor and more tender texture compared to mutton biryani, which can be richer and more robust in taste due to the age of the meat used.

Final Thoughts

Now that you have the keys to making an authentic mutton biryani, it’s time to gather your loved ones and savor this delightful dish! Remember, cooking is all about joy and sharing, so don’t hesitate to make it your own. Enjoy the rich flavors and the warm memories that come with every bite. Happy cooking!
